subject: Consolidating scorecards and tiebreak plan — Liam Carter (SWE II)
snippet: Finalizing panel scores, calling for a tiebreak owner and confirming next steps to recruiter.
messages:
From: Riya Shah <recruiter@talentscout.co>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Candidate scheduling — Liam Carter (SWE II)

Hi Olga (and Jonas),

Quick note — Liam Carter is available for the panel loop next week. I've attached his resume and a completed background note. Interview plan below:
- Tue 7/28 11:00–11:45 AM ET — System design (Jonas)
- Tue 7/28 1:00–1:30 PM ET — Take-home walkthrough (Marissa)
- Wed 7/29 10:00–10:30 AM ET — Behavioral (Olga)

Please confirm availability and whether you want the panel to use the standard scorecard (attached) or a condensed one. Liam's timezone is PST; he prefers morning PT.

Attachments: liam_carter_resume.pdf

Thanks,

Senior Recruiter, TalentScout

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 26 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Candidate scheduling — Liam Carter (SWE II)

Team — thanks Riya for the plan. Confirming I can take the behavioral slot 7/29 10:00 ET. Jonas, Marissa — can you please use the full scorecard (liam_carter-scorecard.xlsx attached) and add 1–2 bullet examples under "tech tradeoffs" / "ownership examples" so we have concrete anchors?

Quick asks for the panel:
- Please fill the scorecard by EOD Wednesday (7/29) — we want to close on Thursday.
- If your score is within 0.5 of another interviewer and you have a strong "no" flag, call it out in the comments field.
- If a tiebreak is needed, we'll escalate to a neutral senior (Jonas, happy to assign if you cannot).

I attached the candidate resume and the standard scorecard anchors we use for SWE II.

Thanks — Olgá (I prefer Olga, but I keep seeing the accent on my name in HR systems)
Olga Petrov
Hiring Manager, Core Systems
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Attachments: liam_carter-scorecard.xlsx, scorecard-anchors.pdf

Done — filled and uploaded my sheet (see liam_carter-scorecard.xlsx, tab: Marissa). Quick notes:
- Strength: clear decomposition of API latency tradeoffs; used example from caching strategy that maps to our prefix cache flow.
- Weakness: limited ownership examples; answers leaned "would pair" rather than "I owned".
- Recommendation: green/lean-hire if we pair with a senior on the infra side — otherwise borderline.

I'll flag a "no" only if any security concern shows up.

–Marissa

> Done — filled and uploaded my sheet (see liam_carter-scorecard.xlsx, tab: Marissa). Quick notes:

Posting a quick reminder — please finalize and lock your scores by EOD today (7/30). Two operational items:
1) If you need help normalizing between low/med/high anchors, see the "scorecard-anchors.pdf" attached (we use the same rubric across IC hires).
2) If the panel ends up with a split (example: 3.5 vs 4.0 vs 3.5), we should pick a tiebreak owner now — Jonas, would you be willing to act as neutral tiebreaker? If not, tag someone in the Eng Leads channel.

Also, for audit: please paste 1–2 verbatim candidate answers you referenced into the scorecard comments so we have evidence in the hiring packet.

Thanks — Tessa (TA ops)
Tessa Morgan
Talent Operations Manager

Attachment: scorecard-anchors.pdf

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Thanks all — saw the uploads. My read: Marissa 4.0, Olga 3.5, Tessa (panel notes) 3.5 — that's effectively a split. I'm fine to be the neutral tiebreaker, but prefer to do a short calibration call (20 min) with the two scoring interviewers tomorrow 8/4 10:00–10:20 ET to review the two contested anchors (ownership example + system tradeoff). If both agree on a final numeric after calibration, we avoid dragging the candidate longer.

If calibration fails, I'll make the call and document the rationale.

Jonas Weber
